newsitem.title: USA: Dole pounds Clinton on foreign contributions.
newsitem.headline: Dole pounds Clinton on foreign contributions.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole took his underdog campaign to New Mexico on Friday, saying he wanted to restore values to the White House instead of "slippery liberalism."

Dole pounded Clinton on the character issue and "scandals" he said highlighted recent stories about questionable contributions to the Democratic Party from people associated with Indonesian, South Korean and other foreign interests.

"Every day we have a new scandal involving the foreign corruption of America. Our elections are not for sale to some foreign influence or some foreign interest. This is the United States of America," Dole told a park rally here.

"Make no mistake about it, a public office is a public trust. And it's time to restore that trust in America and it's time to return values to America in exchange for slippery liberalism in the Clinton administration and bring back common sense and integrity to the White House," he said.

His attack, which drew strong applause, intensified the assault on what Republicans charge is ethical misconduct in the White House. He urged Clinton to "give an accounting" of foreign contributions and said that if the money is tracked, "it rolls all the way down to the (White House) Oval Office."
"He (Clinton) sits there and they give him the money and he gives them a plaque or whatever -- hundreds of thousands of dollars they can't account for," Dole said.
His campaign manager, Scott Reed, was also tough in a statement directed at Clinton: "It's time to stop laundering foreign money and come clean with the American people."

Dole said Clinton's White House did not learn from the Watergate scandal, "which happened on our watch" -- during the Republican Richard Nixon administration. He listed a series of problems including "Travelgate" -- the dismissal of longtime White House employees in the White House travel office.
He also mentioned "Filegate," which involved the reading of FBI files on Republicans by a low level White House employee whom Dole has described as a former bouncer in a bar.
"We're going to get tough with this guy," Dole, who sounded hoarse after a string of rallies and speeches in California before coming to New Mexico, said of Clinton.
New Mexico's Republican Sen. Pete Domenici lauded Dole's effort to attack Clinton on ethics and said Dole should have gone on the offensive earlier.
"He should have made the whole campaign on sleaze," Domenici told Reuters. Later, introducing his longtime friend Dole, Domenici said one of his main character traits was "he always tells the truth."
The rally in a downtown park in the city's oldest section in this Mexico border state attracted several hundred people on a sunny but chilly day.
Clinton carried New Mexico by a narrow margin over President George Bush four years ago and is ahead of Dole in polls now.
Dole planned other rallies on Friday in Wichita, Kansas, and Denver in a grueling schedule before stopping for the night in London, Kentucky.
